plain_english: The first adhyaya opens by defining who is fit to be taught, then presents Dhritarashtra's question about the gathered warriors.
sanskrit_cite: atha prathamo'dhyāyaḥ   vidyāvidyātmanordvayorabhibhāvyābhibhāvakātmakatvaṃ  pradarśayituṃ prathamādhyāyaprastāvaḥ | nahyanutpannavidyāleśāvakāśa upadeśabhājanam nāpi  nirmūlitasamastāvidyāprapañcaḥ ekakoṭiviśrāntasya tu tataḥ  koṭeścyāvayitumaśakyatvāt | ajñaviparyastayostu upadeśyatvaṃ  yaducyate tatkvacideva | tathātvaunmukhyopadeṣṭavye'rthe  sandigdhataiva | ata eva saṃśayanirṇodaka evopadeśa iti  vidyāvidyāṅgasaṃghaṭṭamayaḥ saṃśaya ucyate | devāsurasṛṣṭiśca vidyāvidyāmayīti tatkathopakramaṇameva  mokṣamārgopadeśanam | jñānaṃ ca pradhānaṃ karmāṇi  cāpahartavyānīti karmaṇāṃ jñānaniṣṭhatayā kriyamāṇānāmapi  na bandhakatvamiti jñānaprādhānyam nāntarīyakatvaṃ tu karmaṇām  na tu jñānakarmaṇī samaśīrṣakatayā samuñcīyete ityatra  tātparyam | evameva ca munerabhiprāyaṃ yathāsthānaṃ  pratipādayiṣyāma iti  kimanyaistattvadarśanavighnamātraphalairvāgjālaiḥ | dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca   dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre sarvakṣatrasamāgame | māmakāḥ  pāṇḍavāścaiva kimakurvata sañjaya | atra kecidvyākhyāvikalpamāhuḥ-kurūṇāṃ-karaṇānāṃ  yatkṣetraṃ-anugrāhakam ata eva sāṃsārikadharmāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ  kṣetraṃ-utpattinimittatvāt   ayaṃ sa paramo dharmo yadyogenātmadarśanam (yājñava0 smṛ0)   ityasya ca dharmasya kṣetram samastadharmāṇāṃ  kṣayādapavargaprāptyā trāṇabhūtam tadadhikāri śarīram | sarvakṣetrāṇāṃ kṣaderhiṃsārthatvāt  parasparavadhyaghātakabhāvena vartamānānāṃ  rāgavairāgyakrodhakṣamāprabhṛtīnāṃ samāgamo yatra tasmin  sthitā ye māmakāḥ-avidyāpuruṣocitā avidyāmayāḥ saṅkalpāḥ | pāṇḍavāḥ-śuddhavidyāpuruṣocitā vidyātmanaḥ | te  kimakurvata-kaiḥ khalu ke jitā iti yāvat | mameti kāyatīti  māmakaḥ avidyāpuruṣaḥ | pāṇḍuḥ śuddhaḥ

plain_english: Sanjaya says that seeing the Pandava army arrayed, King Duryodhana approached the teacher and spoke.
sanskrit_cite: sañjaya uvāca   dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavānīkaṃ vyūḍhaṃ duryodhanastadā | ācāryamupasaṅgamya rājā vacanamabravīt

plain_english: Duryodhana asks the teacher to look at the great arrayed army of Pandu's sons, arranged by Drupada's wise son, his disciple.
sanskrit_cite: paśyaitāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāmācārya mahatīṃ camūm | vyūḍhāṃ  drupadaputreṇa tava śiṣyeṇa dhīmatā

plain_english: Here are heroes and great bowmen equal to Bhima and Arjuna in battle: Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great chariot-fighter.
sanskrit_cite: atra śūrā maheṣvāsā bhīmārjunasamā yudhi | yuyudhāno  virāṭaśca drupadaśca mahārathaḥ

plain_english: Dhrishtaketu and Cekitana, the valiant king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaivya, best of men.
sanskrit_cite: dhṛṣṭaketuścekitānaḥ kāśirājaśca vīryavān | purujit  kuntibhojaśca śaivyaśca narapuṅgavaḥ

plain_english: Yudhamanyu and valiant Uttamaujas, Saubhadra, and the Draupadeyas—all indeed great chariot-fighters.
sanskrit_cite: yudhāmanyuśca vikrānta uttamaujāśca vīryavān | saubhadro  draupadeyāśca sarva eva mahārathāḥ

plain_english: But know, best of the twice-born, the distinguished leaders among us, for naming my army's commanders to you.
sanskrit_cite: asmākaṃ tu viśiṣṭā ye tānnibodha dvijottama | nāyakā mama  sainyasya saṃjñārthaṃ tān bravīmi te

plain_english: In the great army, all these hero-approved leaders are: you, Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Shalya, Jayadratha, Ashvatthama, Vikarna, and valiant Saumadatti.
sanskrit_cite: sainye mahati ye sarve netāraḥ śūrasammatāḥ | bhavān bhīṣmaśca  karṇaśca kṛpaḥ śalyo jayadrathaḥ aśvatthāmā vikarṇaśca  saumadattiśca vīryavān

plain_english: And many other heroes, for my sake having abandoned life, armed with various weapons and skilled in various battles, are there.
sanskrit_cite: anye ca bahavaḥ śūrā madarthe tyaktajīvitāḥ | nānāśastrapraharaṇā nāsti nānāyuddhaviśāradāḥ

plain_english: What use is this enumeration? Our force, protected by Bhima, is insufficient; but their force, protected by Bhishma, is sufficient. The Pandava force protected by Bhimasena is ours and insufficient to conquer; or the force protected by Bhishma is related to these Pandavas and sufficient to conquer, if much is not conquerable by them in battle.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃvānena parigaṇanena idaṃ tāvadvastutattvamityāha   aparyāptaṃ tadasmākaṃ balaṃ bhīmābhirakṣitam | paryāptaṃ  tvidameteṣāṃ balaṃ bhīṣmābhirakṣitam | bhīmasenābhirakṣitaṃ pāṇḍavīyaṃ balam  asmākamaparyāptaṃ-jetumaśakyam  athavā-aparyāptaṃ-kiyattadasmadvalasyetyarthaḥ | idaṃ tu  bhīṣmābhirakṣitaṃ balamasmākaṃ saṃbandhi  eteṣāṃ-pāṇḍavānāṃ paryāptaṃ-jetuṃ śakyam yadi vā  paryāptaṃ-bahu na samare jayyametairiti

plain_english: Stationed in all passages according to your portions, you all indeed must protect Bhishma.
sanskrit_cite: ayaneṣu ca sarveṣu yathābhāgamavasthitāḥ | bhīṣmamevābhirakṣantu bhavantaḥ sarva eva hi

plain_english: Causing joy in him, the valiant Kuru elder and grandsire roared loudly and blew the conch.
sanskrit_cite: tasya sañjanayan harṣaṃ kuruvṛddhaḥ pitāmahaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ  vinadyoccaiḥ śaṅkhaṃ dadhmau pratāpavān

plain_english: Then conches, drums, paṇavas, anakas, and gomukhas were struck all at once, and that sound became tumultuous.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śaṅkhāśca bhīryaśca paṇavānakagomukhāḥ | sahasaivābhyahanyanta sa śabdastumulo'bhavat

plain_english: Then Mādhava and the Pāṇḍava, standing in the great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śvetairhayairyukte mahati syandane sthitau | mādhavaḥ  pāṇḍavaścaiva divyau śaṅkhau pradadhmatuḥ

plain_english: Hṛṣīkeśa blew Pāñcajanya, Dhanañjaya blew Devadatta, and Vṛkodara of terrible deeds blew Pauṇḍra, the great conch.
sanskrit_cite: pāñjajanyaṃ hṛṣīkeśo devadattaṃ dhanañjayaḥ | pauṇḍraṃ  dadhmau mahāśaṅkhaṃ bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ

plain_english: King Yudhiṣṭhira, Kuntī's son, blew Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.
sanskrit_cite: anantavijayaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ | nakulaḥ  sahadevaśva sughoṣamaṇipuṣpakau

plain_english: Kāśya, the supreme archer, Śikhaṇḍin, the great chariot-fighter, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa, and the unconquered Sātyaki.
sanskrit_cite: kāśyaśca parameṣvāsaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ | dhṛṣṭadyumno virāṭaśca sātyakiścāparājitaḥ

plain_english: The Pāñcāla great archer, the five Draupadeyas, and mighty-armed Saubhadra each blew conches separately.
sanskrit_cite: pāñcālaśca maheṣvāso draupadeyāśca pañca ye | saubhadraśca  mahābāhuḥ śaṅkhāndadhmuḥ pṛthak pṛthak

plain_english: That sound tore the hearts of Dhartarashtra's sons and resounded tumultuously through sky and earth.
sanskrit_cite: sa ghoṣo dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ hṛdayāni vyadārayat | nabhaśca  pṛthivīṃ caiva tumulo vyanunādayan

plain_english: Then, seeing Dhartarashtra's sons arrayed and weapons begun to clash, the monkey-bannered Pandava raised his bow.
sanskrit_cite: atha vyavasthitāndṛṣṭvā dhārtarāṣṭrānkapidhvajaḥ | pravṛtte  śastrasampāte dhanurudyamya pāṇḍavaḥ

plain_english: Then Arjuna spoke this word to Hrishikesha: O lord of earth, place my chariot between both armies, O Acyuta.
sanskrit_cite: hṛṣīkeśaṃ tadā vākyamidamāha mahīpate | arjuna uvāca   senayorubhayormadhye rathaṃ sthāpaya me'cyuta

plain_english: Until I see these standing eager to fight, with whom by me must be fought in this battle effort.
sanskrit_cite: yāvadetānnirīkṣe'haṃ yoddhrukāmānavasthitān | kairmayā saha  yoddhavyamasmin raṇasamudyame

plain_english: I wish to see those who will fight, who are assembled here, desiring to please evil-minded Dhartarashtra in war.
sanskrit_cite: yotsyamānānavekṣe'haṃ ya ete'tra samāgatāḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrasya durbuddheryuddhe priyacikīrṣavaḥ

plain_english: Sanjaya said: thus addressed by Gudakesha, O Bharata, Hrishikesha placed the best chariot between both armies.
sanskrit_cite: sañjaya uvāca   evamukto hṛṣīkeśo guḍākeśena bhārata | senayorubhayormadhye  sthāpayitvā rathottamam

plain_english: Arjuna said, O Partha, see these gathered Kurus led by Bhishma and Drona.
sanskrit_cite: bhīṣmadroṇapramukhataḥ sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām | uvāca pārtha  paśyaitānsamavetānkurūniti

plain_english: There Partha saw standing fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpaśyatsthitānpārthaḥ pitṛnatha pitāmahān | ācāryānmātulānbhrātṝnputrānpautrānsakhīṃstathā

plain_english: Fathers-in-law and friends were also in both armies.
sanskrit_cite: śvaśurānsuhṛdaścaiva senayorubhayorapi

plain_english: Seeing all those kinsmen standing there, Arjuna was overcome by supreme compassion, sank down, and said this.
sanskrit_cite: tānsamīkṣya sa kaunteyaḥ sarvān bandhūnavasthitān | kṛpayā  parayāviṣṭo sīdamāno'bravīdidam

plain_english: Arjuna said, seeing these kinsmen eager to fight, Krishna, my limbs sink and my mouth dries up.
sanskrit_cite: arjuna uvāca   dṛṣṭvemānsvajanānkṛṣṇa yuyutsūnsamupasthitān | sīdanti mama  gātrāṇi mukhaṃ ca pariśuṣyati

plain_english: Trembling and hair-standing arise in my body; Gandiva slips from my hand, and my skin burns.
sanskrit_cite: vepathuśca śarīre me romaharṣaśca jāyate | gāṇḍīvaṃ sraṃsate  hastāttvakcaiva paridahyate

plain_english: I cannot stand steady, my mind reels, and I see reversed omens, Keśava.
sanskrit_cite: na ca śaknomyavasthātuṃ bhramatīva ca me manaḥ | nimittāni ca  paśyāmi viparītāni keśava

plain_english: I see no good in slaying kin in battle; I do not desire victory, Kṛṣṇa, nor kingdom and pleasures.
sanskrit_cite: na ca śreyo'nupaśyāmi hatvā svajanamāhave | na kāṅkṣe vijayaṃ  kṛṣṇa | na ca rājyaṃ sukhāni ca

plain_english: What is kingdom to us, Govinda, or enjoyments and life, when those for whom we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures are to be slain?
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ no rājyena govinda | kiṃ bhogairjīvitena vā | yeṣāmarthe  kāṅkṣitaṃ no rājyaṃ bhogāḥ sukhāni ca

plain_english: Those standing in battle, abandoning lives and wealth, are teachers, fathers, sons, and grandfathers.
sanskrit_cite: ta ime'vasthitā yuddhe prāṇāṃstyaktvā dhanāni ca | ācāryāḥ  pitaraḥ putrāstathaiva ca pitāmahāḥ

plain_english: I do not wish to kill these kin, even for three-worlds sovereignty or earth; the opponent's view is stated before the answer.
sanskrit_cite: mātulāḥ śvaśurāḥ pautrāḥ syālāḥ sambandhinastathā | etānna  hantumicchāmi ghnato'pi madhusūdana | api trailokyarājyasya hetoḥ kimu mahīkṛte | amī ācāryādayaḥ iti viśeṣabuddhyā buddhāvāropyamāṇā  vadhakarmatayāvaśyaṃ pāpadāyinaḥ | tathā  bhogasukhādidṛṣṭārthametadyuddhaṃ kriyate iti buddhyā  kriyamāṇaṃ yuddheṣvavadhyahananādi tadavaśyaṃ pātakakārīti  pūrvapakṣābhiprāyaḥ | ata eva svadharmamātratayaiva  karmāṇyanutiṣṭha na viśeṣadhiyā-ityuttaraṃ dāsyate

plain_english: Having slain the Dhartarashtrans, what joy would there be, O Janardana?
sanskrit_cite: nihatya dhārtarāṣṭrānnaḥ kā prītiḥ syājjanārdana

plain_english: Sin would cling to us if we killed these aggressors; therefore we are not fit to kill our Dhārtarāṣṭra relatives. In such killing sin alone is the agent; our enemies are already subdued by sin, and killing them along with ourselves would bring sin. Here sin comes from greed and from failing to see faults such as the destruction of family.
sanskrit_cite: pāpamevāśrayedasmān hatvaitānātatāyinaḥ | tasmānnārhā vayaṃ  hantuṃ dhārtarāṣṭrānsvabāndhavān | nihatyeti ātatāyināṃ hanane pāpameva kartṛ | ato'yamarthaḥ  pāpena tāvadete'smacchatravo hatāḥ paratantrīkṛtāḥ tāṃśca  nihatyāsmānapi pāpamāśrayet | pāpamatra lobhavaśāt  kulakṣayādidoṣādarśanam

plain_english: Therefore Arjuna indeed raises the mention of duties such as family destruction: 'How, having killed our own people, could we be happy, O Madhava? Even if these men, their minds overcome by greed, do not see [the fault].'
sanskrit_cite: ata eva kulakṣayādidharmāṇāmupakṣepaṃ karoti arjunaḥ svajanaṃ  hi kathaṃ ityādinā   svajanaṃ hi kathaṃ hatvā sukhinaḥ syāma mādhava | yadyapyete na  paśyanti lobhopahatacetasaḥ

plain_english: How is the fault caused by the destruction of family, and the sin involved in treachery to friends, not to be known by us, so that we may turn away from sin?
sanskrit_cite: kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ mitradrohe ca pātakam | kathaṃ na  jñeyamasmābhiḥ pāpādasmānnivartitum

plain_english: O Janardana, those who clearly see the fault caused by the destruction of a family; when a family is destroyed, its eternal family duties perish.
sanskrit_cite: kulakṣayakṛtaṃ doṣaṃ prapaśyadbhirjanārdana | kulakṣaye  praṇaśyanti kuladharmāḥ sanātanāḥ

plain_english: When dharma is lost, the entire family is overcome by unrighteousness; and from that overcoming of unrighteousness, O Krishna, the women of the family become corrupt.
sanskrit_cite: dharme naṣṭe kulaṃ kṛtsnamadharmo'bhibhavatyuta | adharmābhibhavāt kṛṣṇa | praduṣyanti kulastriyaḥ

plain_english: O Vārṣṇeya, when women are corrupted, varṇa-mixture arises; that mixture leads to hell for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself.
sanskrit_cite: strīṣu duṣṭāsu vārṣṇeya | jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ | saṅkaro  narakāyaiva kulaghnānāṃ kulasya ca

plain_english: The ancestors fall because the rites of rice and water are lost, through the faults of family-destroyers who cause caste mixture.
sanskrit_cite: patanti pitaro hyeṣāṃ luptapiṇḍodakakriyāḥ | doṣairetaiḥ  kulaghnānāṃ varṇasaṅkarakārakaiḥ

plain_english: Eternal birth-duties and family-duties are destroyed; for men whose family duties are destroyed, O Janardana, we have heard that dwelling in hell is certain.
sanskrit_cite: utsādyante jātidharmāḥ kuladharmāśca śāśvatāḥ | utsannakuladharmāṇāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ janārdana | narake niyataṃ vāso bhavatītyanuśuśruma

plain_english: Arjuna says it is a great sin to kill kinsmen out of desire for kingdom pleasure, expressing his own distress.
sanskrit_cite: viśeṣaphalabuddhyā hantavyādiviśeṣabuddhyā ca hananaṃ  mahāpātakamiti | etadeva saṃkṣipyābhidhātuṃ  paritāpātiśayasūcanāyātmagatamevārjuno vacanamāha   aho vata mahatpāpaṃ kartuṃ vyavasitā vayam | yadrājyasukhalobhena  hantuṃ svajanamudyatāḥ | vayamiti - kauravapāṇḍavabhedabhinnāḥ sarva evetyarthaḥ

plain_english: For the discerning one, withdrawal from war is fitting; being killed unarmed by weapon-handed Dhartarashtras in battle would be more beneficial.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ sarveṣvavivekiṣu mama vivekinaḥ kimucitam ucitaṃ  tāvadyuddhānnivartanam etattūcitataramityāha   yadimāmapratīkāramaśastraṃ śastrapāṇayaḥ | dhārtarāṣṭrā  raṇe hanyustanme kṣemataraṃ bhavet

plain_english: Sanjaya said: having spoken thus in battle, Arjuna sat down in the chariot seat, casting aside bow and arrow, his mind distressed with grief.
sanskrit_cite: sañjaya uvāca   evamuktvārjunaḥ saṅkhye rathopastha upāviśat | visṛjya saśaraṃ  cāpaṃ śokasaṃvignamānasaḥ

plain_english: Here is the summary verse: made helpless by the collision of knowledge and ignorance, abandoning both by reason, the sage without discernment becomes; thus in the Gita meaning-gathering composed by Abhinavagupta, first chapter, one, thus auspicious.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   vidyāvidyobhayāghātasaṃghaṭṭa vivaśīkṛtaḥ yuktyā dvayamapi  tyaktvā nirviveko bhavenmuniḥ | iti  śrīmahāmāheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhavadgītārthasaṃgrahe prathamo'dhyāyaḥ | iti śivam
